Map of Hilbert–Smith proof

Map of Hilbert–Smith proof

The proof compares two computations of one invariant. From a hypothetical effective -action the paper constructs a class in controlled -theory over , where is a fixed free -space.

Taking localization boundaries removes the sphere factor and leaves a class over . Over a free space every class has ordinary signatures divisible by (left column). Forgetting the group and turns into the manifold controlled by a degree-one map, whose boundary is (right column).

Both columns end in the same integers, so divides .

Overview

The proof compares two computations of the signature tail of one class .

Theorem 4.3 (blue): any class controlled over a fixed compact free -space has ordinary signatures eventually divisible by . Proposition 13.1 (amber): an effective -action produces such a class whose signatures are eventually .

Blue nodes: proof of the first claim (algebraic). Amber nodes: construction of from the action. Grey: shared machinery. Dashed: cited results.

Highlighted

From to Hilbert–Smith

The classical reduction: once no acts effectively, every compact group acting effectively on a manifold is Lie. Uniform Newman excludes small compact subgroups near the identity, and by Gleason–Yamabe a group without small subgroups is Lie with the given topology. Manifolds with boundary reduce to their interiors; dimension is trivial.

Karoubi localization

Statement

For a small additive category with involution and a Karoubi filtration , ultimate lower quadratic -theory gives a homotopy fibration with natural connecting maps. The connecting map has a relative Poincaré-pair description.

All long exact sequences in the proof arise from this fibration: support Mayer–Vietoris (§4), the finite-support sequence of tail extraction (§3), and the localization boundaries (§6, §12).

Asymptotic category

Statement

Fix with index- subgroups , and a compact metric space on which acts isometrically. An object of is a sequence of finite free based modules , with a free -set and equivariant labels . Morphisms are sequences of equivariant rational matrices, modulo eventual equality, with

Duality transposes matrices. For closed invariant , consists of objects whose labels approach uniformly, and is the exterior quotient.

Role in the proof

Every class in the proof lives in one of these categories. Propagation tending to zero is control at a scale that improves along the sequence, and their -theory behaves like a homology theory of . The index carries both the finite quotients and the mesh . Since equality means eventual equality, errors that tend to zero become exact identities.

How it is proved

and , and transposition preserves propagation. A map factors through exactly when both endpoints of every nonzero entry approach uniformly.

Remarks

Ranks and coefficients are unrestricted; only the degree range of complexes is fixed. That is what later allows averaging over group elements: the propagation of a sum is bounded by the maximum of the propagations, not by their sum.

Statement

is the Witt group of nonsingular invariant symmetric rational forms, and is well defined on it. Its value at is the ordinary signature , and tensoring with a positive definite form multiplies characters.

are spectral subspaces for an invariant inner product, and inertia (projection along a negative subspace) shows independence of choices. A metabolic form has zero signature representation: average to get an invariant complement of the Lagrangian, then replace by to make Lagrangian.

Hilbert–Smith

Statement

A second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group acting continuously and effectively on a connected finite-dimensional manifold is a Lie group with its given topology.

Role in the proof

The classical conclusion, by standard reductions.

How it is proved

The compact -adic reduction and Theorem 1.1 make every compact subgroup Lie. Uniform Newman gives such that a compact Lie group acting on a fixed chart with all displacements acts trivially. Joint continuity gives an identity neighborhood whose subgroups have compact Lie closures with that bound, hence act trivially, hence are trivial by effectiveness. No small subgroups, so the group is Lie by Gleason–Yamabe.

Uses

  • -adic reduction, uniform Newman, Gleason–Yamabe
  • every compact subgroup is Lie

Key steps

1Small subgroups give exact invariance with degree one

The input unavailable for finite groups is (8.1)–(8.6): an open subgroup with displacement , Haar-averaged into an -invariant map of degree one. Everything downstream uses three properties of this data: is invariant, so the action is trivial in the sphere coordinate; has degree one, so the final boundary is one ; and acts freely on , which gives the detector. For a genuine finite cyclic action with small displacement the same machinery proves a local Newman theorem, which is true. The new part is the treatment of the errors of the approximate action: Lemma 9.2, (9.7)–(9.8), Lemma 10.1 and §11.

2First-order coherence suffices over

No higher coherences of the homotopy action are ever built. Splitting needs only , which is an idempotent in , split by Balmer–Schlichting. Symmetric structures need only a strictly self-dual , because has no rational group homology. With rational coefficients, mod- information is recovered from integrality of signatures, through Lemma 3.1.

3Control of the idempotent via free sheets

is not a morphism over : it rotates detector values by . Tensoring with and labeling sheet by cancels the rotation exactly, so lives in the controlled equivariant category. The same compensation is needed for every exterior witness of Lemma 10.1, separately on prefix and suffix. This is the step most specific to this proof.

4Uniform control while

averages terms, and its homotopies terms. This is legitimate because , coefficients are unrestricted, and has propagation zero. So every bound has to be uniform in and in . The carrier method supplies this: bounds come from carrier diameters through a width recursion with steps, independent of rank, valence and subdivision.

5Order of categories and the exterior quotient

exists only on absolute categories, while the corner exists only in an exterior quotient, where the approximate action and the detector make sense. The two are connected by the exterior boundary (Prop. 6.1), which needs and ; here supplies it. Order: corner in , boundaries into , signatures last.

6Computation through the scalar image

is not computed directly. The proof computes in the non-equivariant setting, where homotopy invariance and explicit cut-and-paste are available, and uses that ordinary signatures do not see the difference. has to hold as an identity of -classes in the exterior quotient, where signatures are not defined. It rests on the explicit homotopy isometry of Lemma 5.2.

Consistency checks

Non-effective actions

If the action has a kernel, the small subgroup may fix the chart center. Then , no exists, and the construction stops at (8.4). Effectiveness is used in Lemma 8.1.

Actions through a finite quotient

For acting by rotations, a displacement bound on forces into the kernel, since a nontrivial rotation moves points far. Newman's theorem forces the same in general. So again .

Finite cyclic actions

With and a cyclic -group acting with small displacement and a non-fixed point, the construction applies with and proves a local Newman theorem, which is true. The approximate action is the only new ingredient that requires.

Classical analogue: transfer

If acts freely and orientation-preservingly on a closed oriented -manifold and is invariant, then factors through and . The paper adapts this argument with three changes: degree becomes the signature of the local fibre (the factor makes it a signature), freeness becomes control over , and the action becomes an approximate one with errors tending to zero.
